walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1943 Abraham Maslow drew a triangle of needs.

Bottom: physiological — food, water, sleep. Without these, nothing else matters.

Next up:

  • Safety — a home, health, money.
  • Love & belonging — friends, family.
  • Esteem — respect, achievement.

The top: self-actualisation — becoming the best version of you.

Marketers use this idea — adverts often sell belonging or esteem, not just the product. 🎨

Is a trade deficit necessarily bad?
options: Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
Not necessarily — it can reflect strong domestic demand, attractive investment opportunities, or borrowing to fund growth. Context matters more than the headline figure.
A trade deficit always means a country is losing wealth and failing economically.
A trade deficit means a country has no factories.

mcqs.q: What is asymmetric information as a source of market failure?
options: Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.

When one party in a transaction knows more than the other — leading to problems like adverse selection (used-car market) or moral hazard (insurance). Markets can fail or unravel when information is unequal.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
Asymmetric information means a buyer and seller disagree about a price.

mcqs.q: What components make up aggregate demand?
options: Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
Aggregate demand is just the total amount consumers want to buy.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
AD = C + I + G + (X - M): consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. A shift in any component shifts the AD curve.
